key_concepts: Roots anchor plants firmly in the soil
Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil
Roots store food in some plants
Two main root system types are taproot and fibrous
Taproot and fibrous root systems differ in structure and function
Root crops include radish, sweet potato, taro, and cassava
The shoot system includes the stem, leaves, and other above-ground structures
Stems and leaves have functions that support plant growth and survival
Leaf structures and veins can be observed closely
Root growth can be affected by soil type, light, and watering frequency
